rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Imam says the Prophet knew the accusation was false; the order was meant to make the woman repent, and Ali would have carried out a binding command.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن بكير قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام جعلت فداك كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أمر بقتل القبطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports implicate additional people in the accusation; the eunuch Jarih was Maria's servant, sent with her by the ruler of Egypt.
rows.anchor: روايات أخر تدل على مشاركة غيرها معها في هذا الرمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai doubts these accounts because their story does not fit the Qur'anic account, unless the narrations give only an abbreviated version.
rows.anchor: هذه الروايات لا تخلو من نظر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses describe a connected group spreading slander to disgrace the Prophet, with people repeating it for a time and disregarding his God-given honor.
rows.anchor: كان هناك جماعة مرتبط بعضهم ببعض يذيعون الحديث ليفضحوا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the story would require a punishment that was not carried out, Tabatabai holds that the slander penalty verse came later; the scandal passage first established innocence without witnesses and prohibited slander.
rows.anchor: أن آيات الإفك نزلت قبل آية حد القذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the penalty already applied, its long delay and waiting for revelation are inexplicable; if revealed together, the scandal passage would refer to it or adjoin its verse, especially given its threats.
rows.anchor: ولو كان حد القاذف مشروعا قبل حديث الإفك لم يكن هناك مجوز لتأخيره مدة معتدا بها وانتظار الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The timing problem is sharper if the penalty verse descended with the scandal passage: two punishments would have been due, yet only one would have been revealed.
rows.anchor: يتأكد الإشكال على تقدير نزول آية القذف مع نزول آيات الإفك فإن لازمه أن يقع الابتلاء بحكم الحدين فينزل حكم الحد الواحد

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A person who says about a believer only what his eyes saw and ears heard is among those described as loving indecency to spread among believers.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال من قال في مؤمن ما رأته عيناه وسمعته أذناه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that publicizing an indecency is like initiating it.
rows.anchor:
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
" من أذاع فاحشة كان كمبتدئها "

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عائشة، ابن زيد
rows.claim: One reported occasion for the command not to withhold charity is Abu Bakr's stopping support for his cousin Mistah after the slander, then resuming it after the verse and affirming his wish for God's forgiveness.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وعائشة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Another report says a group of Companions swore not to give charity or support to a man who had spoken in the slander; al-Tabari and Ibn Mardawayh transmit it from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: نزلت في جماعة من الصحابة أقسموا على أن لا يتصدقوا على رجل تكلم بشيء من الإفك ولا يواسوهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: In Abu al-Jarud's report, the recipients include the Messenger's relatives, the poor, and emigrants; believers should pardon one another so God may show them mercy and forgive them.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { ولا يأتل أولوا الفضل منكم والسعة أن يؤتوا أولي القربى }

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: The penalty for accusing chaste women was revealed in Medina; God excludes persistent slanderers from the designation of faith and calls them sinners, linking this to Iblis's disobedience and the curse on accusers.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في حديث قال ونزل بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objectors reason that if humans like the Prophet can receive revelation through angels or direct speech from God, they too should receive angels or see God.
rows.anchor: لو كانت الرسالة - وهي نزول الملائكة بالوحي أو تكليمه تعالى البشر بالمشافهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their unqualified demand for angels or sight of God supports this reading; earlier they had asked for an angel to accompany the Prophet as a warner, which would certify him.
rows.anchor: إطلاق إنزال الملائكة ورؤية الرب من غير أن يقولوا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة فيصدقوك أو نرى ربنا فيصدقك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God 'our Lord' is taunting: polytheists did not regard Him as their own lord, since they worshipped other lords while recognizing God as Lord of lords.
rows.anchor: في التعبير عنه تعالى بلفظ ربنا نوع تهكم منهم فإن المشركين ما كانوا يرونه تعالى ربا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They chose idols over the angels and celestial spirits they associated with them because idols were tangible and present for worship and offerings.
rows.anchor: عدلوا عن عبادة أرباب الأصنام وهم الملائكة وروحانيات الكواكب ونحوهم إلى عبادة الأصنام والتماثيل لتكون محسوسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand expresses unjust self-aggrandizement and grave transgression.
rows.anchor: أي أقسم لقد طلبوا الكبر لأنفسهم بغير حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hijr means something forbidden or prohibited; the Qur'anic phrase reflects a customary protective formula spoken by someone facing a feared person.
rows.anchor: في المفردات الحجر الممنوع منه بتحريمه قال تعالى { وقالوا هذه أنعام وحرث حجر }

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says that in the pre-Islamic sacred months, a man fearing someone might say hijran mahjuran to forbid an attack during that month.
rows.anchor: وعن الخليل كان الرجل يرى الرجل الذي يخاف منه القتل في الجاهلية في الأشهر الحرم فيقول حجرا محجورا

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda calls it a protective formula used by someone fearing another in the sanctuary or a sacred month when they meet with a grievance between them.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عبيدة هي عوذة للعرب يقولها من يخاف آخر في الحرم أو في شهر حرام إذا لقيه وبينهما ترة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day phrase modifies 'no glad tidings'; the second 'that day' confirms it, and 'no' negates glad tidings categorically. The criminals here are chiefly the polytheists who deny the meeting with God.
rows.anchor: يوم - على ما قيل - ظرف لقوله { لا بشرى } وقوله { يومئذ } تأكيد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai prefers the polytheists as the speakers: seeing angels coming to punish, they ask for protection, which the phrase cannot secure.
rows.anchor: فاعل يقولون هم المشركون أي يقول المشركون يومئذ للملائكة وهم قاصدوهم بالعذاب حجرا محجورا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the speakers to be the angels, telling the polytheists that glad tidings, entry into Paradise, or refuge from punishment are forbidden; Tabatabai finds the first reading nearer the context.
rows.anchor: وقيل ضمير الجميع للملائكة، والمعنى ويقول الملائكة للمشركين حراما محرما عليكم سماع البشرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nathr means dispersal; the disbelievers' deeds become useless like scattered dust, an image of God's overpowering annulment of their works, as if a victor destroyed every trace of an enemy's house and possessions.
rows.anchor: والنثر التفريق. والمعنى وأقبلنا إلى كل عمل عملوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction between deeds being annulled at resurrection and other verses saying unbelief nullified them in life: after death their already-hidden nullity becomes manifest to them.
rows.anchor: ولا منافاة بين ما تدل عليه الآية من حبط الأعمال يومئذ وبين ما تدل عليه آيات أخر أن أعمالهم أحبطت حينما عملوها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden's people are the Godfearing, as the preceding passage identifies the promised eternal Garden as theirs; mustaqarr and maqil refer to places of residence and rest.
rows.anchor: المراد بأصحاب الجنة المتقون فقد تقدم قوله قبل آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qaylula is midday rest, with or without sleep; Paradise has no sleep.
rows.anchor: ومن القيلولة وهي الاستراحة في منتصف النهار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say 'better' and 'more beautiful' lose their comparative force here, as in the cited verses; Tabatabai allows that they retain comparison, since even by the sinners' own supposed standards the Garden is better than the Fire, and also reports a satirical reading.
rows.anchor: وكلمتا { خير } و { أحسن } منسلخان عن معنى التفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase likely depends on an omitted command, 'remember the day'; its identification as resurrection follows from the next verse's 'that day.' Other proposed attachments add nothing.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن الظرف منصوب بفعل مقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tashaqqaqu is originally tatashaqqaqu, from the form meaning a split or opening; ghamaam names cloud for covering sunlight, and the preposition can mean either accompanying cloud or opening from it.
rows.anchor: و { تشقق } أصله تتشقق من باب التفعل من الشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky appears to split with its cloud covering and its angelic inhabitants descending, like the scene in al-Haqqah; it may also figuratively disclose the hidden heavenly realm and its inhabitants to earthly people.
rows.anchor: فالآية قريبة المعنى من قوله في موضع آخر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says the cloud itself splits the sky, as in the verse about God coming in canopies of cloud with angels and the matter being decided.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد أن السماء يشقها الغمام وهو الذي يذكره في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the event 'splitting' rather than simply opening heightens its awe, and the indefinite accusative tanwin in tanzilan magnifies the descent.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عن الواقعة بالتشقق دون التفتح وما يماثله للتهويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absolute sovereignty truly belongs to the Merciful on that day because causes and their links to effects fail; resurrection reveals that God alone always owned rule and command, while worldly appearances had suggested independent causes.
rows.anchor: أي الملك المطلق يومئذ حق ثابت للرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is hard for disbelievers because they relied on transient appearances and earthly life, cut themselves off from the true owner of sovereignty and lasting life, and have no refuge.
rows.anchor: الوجه فيه ركونهم إلى ظواهر الأسباب وإخلادهم إلى الحياة الأرضية البائدة الداثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mulk is the subject and al-haqq its definite predicate to signal restriction; the time phrase marks when that predicate appears. Ownership is always God's, but apparent creaturely ownership ends at resurrection.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا يكون الملك مبتدأ والحق خبره عرف لإفادة الحصر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Other parses make al-mulk mean ownership with the day attached to it, attach the day to an omitted description of al-haqq, identify it as God's day, or make the day the predicate; Tabatabai calls these weak and unhelpful.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم الملك بمعنى المالكية ويومئذ متعلق به والحق خبر الملك

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Sulayman ibn Khalid reports from Imam al-Sadiq that the disbelievers' works had been bright as Egyptian cotton, but they never abandoned forbidden acts when these arose; Tabatabai says this meaning recurs through several routes from him and his father.
rows.anchor: عن سليمان بن خالد قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا }

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: In a report on the believer's grave, the two angels enlarge it to the eye's reach, open a door to Paradise, and tell him to sleep peacefully like a pampered youth.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الأعلى وبإسناد آخر عن سويد بن غفلة قال قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام في حديث وضع المؤمن في قبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report treats this verse as describing the intermediate realm and its instruction to sleep explains why the verse calls Paradise a midday resting place.
rows.anchor: والرواية - كما ترى - تجعل الآية من آيات البرزخ

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas's account says Uqba ibn Abi Muayt hosted the Prophet, accepted the testimony required before eating, then spat at him at his friend Ubayy ibn Khalaf's urging; Uqba was captured at Badr and executed.
rows.anchor: أخرج أبو نعيم من طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس قال كان عقبة بن أبي معيط لا يقدم من سفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports identifying the path the wrongdoer wishes he had taken with the Messenger as Ali are inner Qur'anic meaning or application, not the verse's exegesis.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في غير واحد من الروايات في قوله تعالى { يقول يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding statement about taking desire as god is summarized by the verse about being unable to make those in graves hear, and elaborated in the verse about one who makes desire his god and is sealed from guidance.
rows.anchor: وما أنت بمسمع من في القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The natural syntax makes ilahahu the first object of ittakhadha and hawahu the second: they rightly recognize an obeyed deity but wrongly make desire, rather than truth, their authority.
rows.anchor: أي إن { اتخذ } فعل متعد إلى مفعولين

rows.speaker: عدة من المفسرين
rows.claim: A number of commentators instead make hawahu the first object and ilahahu the delayed second object, explaining the order as emphasis or exclusivity; Tabatabai rejects this as ill-suited to the context.
rows.anchor: أن { هواه } مفعول أول لقوله { اتخذ } و { إلهه } مفعول ثان مقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am is disjunctive, hisab means supposition, and the plural pronouns refer semantically to the relative clause in the previous verse.
rows.anchor: أم منقطعة، والحسبان بمعنى الظن وضمائر الجمع راجعة إلى الموصول في الآية السابقة باعتبار المعنى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People reach life's felicity either by reasoning to recognize and follow truth or, if unable to reason independently, by hearing and following someone who knows and advises them.
rows.anchor: وسيلة الإنسان إلى سعادة الحياة أحد أمرين إما أن يستقل بالتعقل فيعقل الحق فيتبعه أو يرجع إلى قول من يعقله وينصحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether most can hear truth or reason it out and follow it; the answer explains that they do neither, like livestock that cannot grasp meaning beyond sounds.
rows.anchor: بل أتظن أن أكثرهم لهم استعداد استماع الحق ليتبعه أو استعداد عقل الحق ليتبعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are more astray than livestock because animals avoid what harms them, while these people prefer harm to benefit; animals also lack the human equipment for guidance that people possess.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الأنعام لا تقتحم على ما يضرها وهؤلاء يرجحون ما يضرهم على ما ينفعهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some infer from the comparison that livestock have no knowledge of their Lord.
rows.anchor: واستدل بعضهم بالآية على أن الأنعام لا علم لها بربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabatabai says the verse denies neither basic knowledge of God in livestock nor in disbelievers; it denies disbelievers' following innate rational truth, which desire has veiled, and compares them with livestock lacking that kind of perception.
rows.anchor: إن الآية لا تنفي عنها ولا عن الكفار أصل العلم بالله وإنما تنفي عن الكفار اتباع الحق الذي يهدي إليه عقل الإنسان الفطري

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another answer says the wording speaks only according to outward appearance; Tabatabai says that claim cannot be established by argument.
rows.anchor: وأما ما أجاب به بعضهم أن الكلام خارج مخرج الظاهر فقول لا سبيل إلى إثباته بالاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following nine verses illustrate that the Messenger guides people toward right conduct: some accept God's guidance, while those who make desire their god cannot be guided by anyone apart from Him.
rows.anchor: هاتان الآيتان وما بعدهما إلى تمام تسع آيات في معنى التنظير لما تضمنته الآيتان السابقتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rahman is the predicate of an omitted 'He'; the following command branches from it, the bā makes the question transitive while implying concern, and khabiran is circumstantial. The sense is to ask the Merciful, who sustains creation and knows reality, about the true state of affairs.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الرحمن خبرا لمبتدأ محذوف والتقدير هو الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an idiom assuring the truth of what was stated, like telling someone to ask and receive the answer or saying that they have come to the expert.
rows.anchor: فقوله { فاسأل به خبيرا } كناية عن أن الذي أخبر به حقيقة الأمر التي لا معدل عنها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One alternative makes al-Rahman a detached nominative used for praise; Tabatabai says the divergent parses generally do not fit the context.
rows.anchor: فقيل إن الرحمن مرفوع على القطع للمدح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative treats al-Rahman as the subject and fas'al bihi as its predicate; Tabatabai rejects the scattered alternatives as contextually unsuitable.
rows.anchor: وقيل مبتدأ خبره قوله { فاسأل به }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative makes al-Rahman the predicate of the relative pronoun at the beginning of the verse; Tabatabai rejects the divergent parses as contextually unsuitable.
rows.anchor: وقيل خبر مبتدؤه { الذي } في صدر الآية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative reads al-Rahman as an apposition to the implicit pronoun in istawa; Tabatabai rejects the scattered alternatives as contextually unsuitable.
rows.anchor: وقيل بدل من الضمير المستكن في { استوى }.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view makes fas'al bihi the predicate of al-Rahman and calls the fa explanatory; Tabatabai rejects the scattered alternatives as contextually unsuitable.
rows.anchor: وقيل في { فاسأل به } إنه خبر للرحمن كما تقدم والفاء فصيحة،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view treats fas'al as a separate consequential sentence and varies whether the bā is a particle of relation or means 'about,' with the pronoun referring either to God or to the preceding creation and establishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل جملة مستقلة متفرعة على ما قبلها والفاء للتفريع ثم الباء في

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reading makes khabiran circumstantial of a pronoun referring to God, so the command means to ask God while He is knowledgeable; Tabatabai finds the alternatives unsuitable to the context.
rows.anchor: وقيل { خبيرا } حال عن الضمير وهو راجع إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading makes khabiran the object and bā mean 'about'; the expert is variously identified as God, Gabriel, Muhammad, readers of earlier scriptures, or anyone acquainted with these realities.
rows.anchor: وقيل مفعول فاسأل والباء بمعنى عن والمعنى فاسأل عن الرحمن أو عن حديث الخلق والاستواء خبيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to prostrate begins another instance of hostility toward the Prophet's true call: they arrogantly refuse it; mentioning al-Rahman links the verse to the preceding description, likely with the definite article referring back to it.
rows.anchor: هذا فصل آخر من معاملتهم السوء مع الرسول ودعوته الحقة يذكر فيه استكبارهم عن السجود لله سبحانه
